original_annotations.narration: Zest the lemon against the grater using the right hand to hold the lemon and rotating it to make sure that the lemon is zested equally and holding the grater in the left hand steady.
Shake hands slightly to remove some cramp.
Tap the lemon against the grater to remove any loose zest from it.
Pick up the grater using the left hand.
Place the zested lemon down onto the countertop using the right hand.
pick up the serrated knife on the counter top using the right hand.
Turn over the grater using both hands.
Scrape the zest from the inside of the grater using the back of the knife in the right hand, whilst holding the grater in the left hand.
Tap the serrated knife against the saucer to remove the zest from inside the grater.
Scrape out the zest from the inside of the grater using the back of the serrated knife in the right hand.
Tap the serrated knife against the saucer to remove the zest from it.
Rotate the grater in both hands to get access to the other end.
Scrape out the zest from the inside of the grater using the back of the knife in the right hand.
tap the knife against the side of the saucer remove the zest from it
Repeatedly tap the inside of the grater using the knife to remove the zest on the outside of the grater into the saucer below it.
Drag the knife down the outside part of the grater to remove the zest from it, but also making sure that the knife doesn't get damaged, or the grater gets damaged.
Rotate the way that the grater was held so that the other diagonal can be accessed using the knife easier.
repeatedly tap the inside of the grater using the knife to remove the zest that has been loosened and hopefully place it into the saucer below it.
Shake the grater to remove some zest from it.
Bash the end of the knife against the top of the grater to remove the zest from the side of the grater into the saucer.

observed_events.description: A box grater is held while a lemon is rubbed against its fine face over a saucer. Later a red-handled serrated knife is picked up and its back is used to scrape or tap zest from inside the inverted box grater. The knife is newly held, but it is not the tool that originally removed the outer zest.

equivalence_review.policy: Accept a real listing supplying the visible freestanding box-grater type with a publicly visible fine-zesting face. Any brand, colour or size and same-type multipacks are allowed; one cart listing is requested, not an unstated exact physical-unit quantity. Integrated/removable collecting containers are accessories. Reject a separate different utensil bundled with it, flat/container-top graters and publicly coarse/medium-only tools. Missing evidence for a fine face remains unknown, not disproven.
